hardware: AMD RYZEN AI MAX+ PRO 395 / Radeon 8060S (laptop; gross numbers; provisional pending the desktop gfx1151)
change: IQ3_S joins the dense raw-IQ integer-MMQ route, and IQ4_NL is un-held. GGUF_IQ_DENSE_MMQ_PREFILL_POLICY now routes all four quants whose K32 groups are expressible as scale*int8: IQ4_XS, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S, IQ4_NL.

iq3_s_implementation.expansion: iq3_s_expand_group32: one 4-bit scale per K32 group, eight grid lookups of four values each with a per-value sign bit. Grid magnitudes are odd 1..15 so the signed residual fits int8 with wide margin. words[w] byte b carries element 4*w+b, so the grid slot is exactly w.
iq3_s_implementation.table: The 2 KB IQ3_S grid was extracted from gguf_iq_dense.hip into gguf_iq3_s_grid.h and is now included by both kernels, so there is one copy rather than two. gguf_iq_dense.py's TABLE_HASH covers the new header; the dense 84-case exact-parity gate passed unchanged after the extraction, confirming it is bit-exact.
iq3_s_implementation.leaf_correctness: max relative error 0.0047-0.0097 at correlation 0.999983 against the strict GEMV across every measured shape and row count

retained_trade.protocol: published README sweep protocol, 512/128, and context512 teacher gate with 18 prompts x 9 forced steps in the production config
retained_trade.delta: prefill 127.20 -> 171.86 tok/s (+35.1%); decode unchanged (rows=1 is below min_rows)
retained_trade.honest_reading: Mean regresses 36% and p95 52% against the two-quant policy. The maximum improves to 0.0297407, the best of the four arms and better than the previous default's 0.0354152. Both binding gates pass; the strict mean/p95/p99 thresholds were already failing before this change, the pre-existing campaign state. This is retained as a production-profile trade under the standing instruction to take production-correct wins, and is rolled back per quant by deleting a policy entry.

why_not_a_localizable_defect: IQ4_NL and IQ3_S were each held out briefly on the mean regression. A per-tensor localization of the IQ4_NL cost was attempted and failed: excluding the three early ffn_down tensors, which a single-prompt probe blamed for 71% of the divergence-from-default, measured no better against the teacher (mean 0.0013632 against 0.0013457 for all seven). Against the teacher the cost is not attributable to particular tensors, so it is a systematic mean/tail-shape property of the shared Q8_1 DS4 activation plane rather than a defect to localize.
still_on_the_strict_gemv: Q3_K, IQ2_S and IQ2_XS carry a scale per 16 elements; under the per-32 contract their residual integers reach +/-128 and +/-1333 and do not fit int8. Routing them needs a per-16-scale MMQ contract, i.e. a kernel redesign rather than an expansion function.

campaign_cumulative.prefill_tok_s: 22.1 (start) -> 29.9 (per-tensor repack veto) -> 41.5 (dense T16 role coverage) -> 127.2 (dense IQ MMQ) -> 171.9 (four-quant) = 7.78x
campaign_cumulative.gap_to_plain_same_host_same_protocol: 13.3x -> 1.72x (plain Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_S is 294.8 tok/s on this laptop)

correctness_suites: tests/test_gguf_iq_dense_mmq_route.py (32 cases), test_gguf_iq_source_mmq_prefill.py, test_gguf_ud_dense.py (84-case exact parity, unchanged by the table extraction), test_gfx1151_backend.py, test_gguf_e2e_acceptance.py, test_gguf_ud_km.py, test_gguf_ud_ks.py all green
limitations: The mean/p95 regression is real and recorded; if a task or repeat/serving gate later shows it matters, roll back per quant (IQ4_NL buys +22%, IQ3_S +8.3%).
The open improvement is a finer activation quantization than the shared DS4 plane, which would likely recover the mean.
Gated on K_M only. K_S carries 15 IQ3_S tensors against K_M's 4, so its gain should be larger and its numerics were not separately gated.

DECISION_REFERENCE_CORRECTION_2026_09_09.verdict: The four-quant integer-MMQ policy this artifact retains EXCEEDS the binding 5e-2 absolute maximum-row ceiling (0.170390 at one row) when scored against strict. The 'maximum improves to 0.0297407, the best of the four arms' claim below is an artifact of the teacher reference and does not hold against strict, where it is the worst by 7x. The retention decision needs re-taking on this data.
